To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CD4+ T lymphocytes from tuberculosis patients exhibit a distinct gene expression profile and the expression of BAFF/APRILL is significantly elevated.
we have identified a set of transcriptional signatures of CD4+T cells that can be used as a diagnostic tool for the diagnosis of active tuberculosis.

we have identified a set of transcriptional signatures and cytokines that can be used as biomarkers for active tuberculosis and that the B cell activating factor of the TNF family and a proliferation-inducible ligand are upregulated in the disease stage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and validation of CD4+ Th cell-related biomarkers in human active pulmonary tuberculosis and the potential role of BAFF and/or APRIL in the disease process.
the development of novel biomarkers for the diagnosis of active pulmonary tuberculosis.
the identification and characterization of novel immune biomarkers and their potential use in the diagnosis of tuberculosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BAFF and APR IL are the most important factors in the diagnosis of tuberculosis.
our findings provide new insights into the molecular mechanism underlying the pathogenesis of active TB and suggest the potential of BAFF/APRILL as a biomarker of active TB.
the CD4+ T-cell gene expression profiles and cytokines in peripheral blood and pleural effusions are useful for the diagnosis of tuberculosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the BAFF/BLyS and APRIL/TALL-1 system may play an important role in the pathophysiology of active TB, and that the expression levels of these proteins in serum and pleurisy could be utilized as diagnostic tools.
the CD4+ T lymphocyte gene expression profile is associated with the development of active tuberculosis.
we have identified the BAFF/APRL system to be a novel biomarker of human active pulmonary tuberculosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD4+ T lymphocyte gene expression profiling may be a useful approach for identifying biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
the BAFF system may be a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of TB.
the BAFF and APR IL system is a potential diagnostic marker for tuberculosis.
